observations: Two large solar panels leaning against a wall.
The panels feature a half-cut cell design with a horizontal dividing line.
Cells appear to be monocrystalline based on the dark color.
No manufacturer label or specification sticker is visible on the front.
A watermark 'SMART ENERGIES' is present on the image.

claims.evidence: The specifications mentioned by the seller are not included in the provided text or visible in the photo.

risks.proof: A clear photo of the specification label on the back of the panel.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a low-wattage (e.g., 250W) generic panel.

risks.risk: Unknown brand and manufacturing quality tier.
risks.proof: A photo of the back label showing the manufacturer's name.

risks.risk: Internal cell damage or micro-cracks not visible to the eye.
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter test of the Open Circuit Voltage (Voc) and Short Circuit Current (Isc) in direct sunlight.

proof_requests: Photo of the technical specification label on the back of the panel.
Close-up photos of the panel surface to check for glass chips or cell cracks.
Video showing a multimeter test of the panel's output in sunlight.
response.reason: The wattage, voltage, and brand—which are the primary factors determining the value of a solar panel—are not visible in the photo and are typically found on a label on the rear.
